resources.string: SPOOF: preview and edit a port
Follow the highlighted objective, or restart this lesson.
Connect start 0 to extraction 6. The two ports inside a domino connect automatically; every outside contact must match. Let us practice.
Press ROTATE once. The preview shows the orientation and port order. Four rotations return to the original position.
Place [0 | 2] vertically at the marked cell beside start (column 2, row 4). Port 0 must touch start 0.
One domino per turn. Press EXECUTE TURN to resolve the system and refill resources.

RAM returns to 3. Trace rises by 8 plus noise. At 100 you lose. Revealed honeypots add 20 noise and discard a script when triggered; the daemon follows connected hardware toward start. Defeats are checked before victory.
Execute PING (1 RAM, no noise). It reveals hidden honeypots and the next three available dominoes.
Inspect the revealed honeypot and hardware preview. PING information lasts until the next turn for hardware; traps stay revealed.
Select SPOOF, then [3 | 2]. Choose the first port, value 0, and apply. Cost: 2 RAM and 5 noise.
The hardware is now [0 | 2]. SPOOF changes a port permanently. In normal play you can choose either port and any value from 0 to 6.
Select KILL_PROCESS and tap the marked firewall beside start. Cost: 3 RAM and 15 noise.
The firewall is removed and its cell is available for hardware. RAM is empty until the next turn.
Select BRIDGE, keep horizontal orientation, and tap the marked firewall between the two ports with value 2. Cost: 2 RAM and 10 noise.
The bridge connects equal ports across the firewall without removing it. Vertical bridges work the same way above and below a firewall.
Final practice: connect start to extraction and execute the turn to win. You can act freely. Prefer matching route hardware along the middle row; consult PROTOCOL whenever needed.
Tutorial complete! You are ready for a new network.
This match ended. Retry or return to the menu.
You already placed hardware. Execute the turn.
Select hardware from your current hand.
Both ports must fit inside the board. Rotate or choose another cell.
Match every touching outside port; try rotating the hardware.
Place next to the network connected to start.
Not enough RAM. Place hardware and execute the turn to refill it.
Choose a valid target: a hand port for SPOOF, a firewall for KILL, or equal ports across a firewall for BRIDGE.
Place one domino before executing the turn.
Trace reached 100. Use fewer noisy scripts.
No placement can continue this network.
Challenge failed: the turn or trace limit was exceeded.

Connect S0 (start, value 0) to X6 (extraction, value 6), then execute the turn. Match every outside contact; the two halves inside a domino connect automatically. Green outlines mark valid origins for the selected domino. Tap an origin to place its first port there; the other goes right or down.

██: firewall, blocks placement. HP: revealed honeypot; covering a hidden or revealed trap adds 20 noise and discards a script (once per placement, only for new traps). D!: daemon, moves one connected cell toward start each turn; reaching start ends the match. ═ / ║: horizontal / vertical bridge across a firewall.

At 100 trace you lose. Running out of hardware or having no legal placements without an available SPOOF also ends the match. Defeats from trace or daemon are checked before victory.
Scripts spend RAM when executed successfully. You have up to 3 RAM, restored after executing the turn. Placing and rotating hardware cost no RAM. You can read help even when a script is unavailable.
Trace rises by 8 plus pending noise each time you execute the turn. At 100 you lose, even if you connected extraction that turn. Spend fewer turns and use noisy scripts carefully.
Place exactly one domino per turn. You may also execute scripts while you have RAM, before or after placing it. Execute the turn to resolve the system and continue.
Noise accumulates from scripts and newly triggered honeypots. It is added to the base 8 trace when you execute the turn, then resets for the next turn. Reading help adds no noise.
This number identifies the generated network and starting decks. Retry last seed in the menu starts the same challenge again; it does not resume your previous match.

Select a script to use its effect. PING runs immediately; other scripts require a target. Each successful execution consumes the card and its RAM cost and adds its noise. Cancel a pending selection without spending resources. Use the ? beside each card for instructions.

Each domino has two ports with values from 0 to 6; a blank half means 0. Select a domino, rotate if needed, then tap a green outlined cell. Both cells must be free and every outside contact must match. The placement must touch the network connected to S0.

Cycles through horizontal, vertical, reversed horizontal and reversed vertical. The preview shows the exact port order: first on the left or top. Four presses restore the original orientation. Rotation spends no resources.

Available after placing one domino. Applies 8 plus noise to trace, moves the daemon and checks defeat and victory. If play continues, restores 3 RAM, draws one domino and up to one script if there is room and stock, and clears the PING hardware preview.

Tap the card to reveal all hidden honeypots and up to three upcoming dominoes immediately. Traps stay revealed; the domino preview lasts until you execute the turn. Revealing traps does not trigger them.

Select the card, then a domino in your hand. Choose either port and a value from 0 to 6. Check the before/after images and apply to change that port permanently. Cancel or close to leave the domino and resources unchanged.
Select the card, then tap a firewall to remove it and free its cell for hardware. This script targets firewalls; it cannot remove the daemon.

Select the card, choose horizontal or vertical, then tap a firewall. The two ports on opposite sides must exist and have equal values. The bridge connects them without removing the firewall. Each firewall can hold one bridge.
Ten deterministic puzzles. Win one to unlock the next.
